findings.claim: The record count assertion went from == 11 to >= 11, so ADR 0012 (or any later record) could be deleted without this test noticing; pin it at == 12.
ADR 0012 says the docs' install lines still name main until the first release, but the three uv tool install lines name no ref at all; only the two uses: lines name @main.

verdict.text: The change is a close port of loop-harness's release flow, minus the floor and ST-11 parts, and it should run on GitHub.
I simulated the first 0.2.0 run's shell steps locally and every one worked.
Nothing blocks.
Two small fixes: one test assertion got weaker, and one sentence in the ADR is slightly wrong.

Gates: `loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree reported lint, format, tests and integration all pass, eval rows r1 to r7 all pass, and "stamp green: 59ad6b558cf5a316e354a4307cedef7a5de4fb88318c6e346ac3756df8828cc8".
I also ran `uv run pytest -q` (445 passed, 11 deselected), `uv run ruff check` and `uv run ruff format --check` myself.
All are clean, and no test takes over 1s by `--durations`, so no `slow` marker was needed.
CI conditions: I ran the full suite with `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` and a fresh HOME, with only `uv` and `/usr/bin:/bin` on PATH (no claude, no just).
445 passed.
The release.yml test job will not trip on a missing git identity or tool on ubuntu-latest.
First-release simulation, in a scratch copy of the tree: `next_release_version.py PATCH --version 0.2.0` printed 0.2.0.
Without `--version` it refused.
`release.py set 0.2.0` wrote the manifest, README.md, the tutorial and the how-to, and changed no other file.
That matches the bump job's `git add` line, so its `git diff --exit-code` check passes.
`uv build` gave kmctl-0.2.0 wheel and sdist.
`uvx twine check`, `check_wheel.py` and `smoke_wheel.py --version 0.2.0` all passed, and so did the SHA256SUMS step.
The release-tag compare path (`git worktree add` of the previous commit, `release.py --repo ... current`, then `compare`) gave 0.1.0 to 0.2.0, verdict raised.
`is-prerelease 0.2.0` exited 1.
The `PREVIOUS` pipeline gives an empty string with no prior tag (it falls through `|| true` under pipefail), so `--notes-start-tag` is left out.
Workflows against the reference: the pinned SHAs match loop-harness's exactly.
release-tag.yml differs from the reference only in the dropped floor/ST-11 step, the build without SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION, twine check moved into the build step, and the tag message.
Permissions: read-only at the top level, `contents: write` plus `pull-requests: write` on bump, and `contents: write` on tag.
A merge by a human starts release-tag, and this ticket's own landing does not touch plugin.json, so it starts no release.
Eval rows: I read each test against its fails_when.
r1 checks pyproject's dynamic version, the regex source path and a real `uv build` at both 0.1.0 and a changed 9.8.7.
r2 covers current, set (manifest plus all 5 refs, moving off an older tag), refusal with nothing written, the four compare verdicts, is-prerelease, and no commit or tag.
r3 uses real tmp_path repos for each increment and for the no-tag refusal.
r4 uses offline fake wheels for each failure mode.
r5 checks trigger and inputs, step order, that the staged set includes the manifest and all docs, no PyPI, 40-char SHAs, and writer-only permissions.
r6 checks the ADR's schema, the names it must contain, the overview, the upgrade step and `kmctl check`.
None of these tests asserts a constant or mocks away the thing under test.
Docs: the how-to's upgrade step uses commands that exist (`kmctl plugin update` and `status` are real verbs).
Its `uv tool install --force ...@vX.Y.Z` placeholder does not match `_INSTALL`, so `set` still finds exactly 5 lines.
The "ref" prose in step 3 holds both before and after the first version PR.
f1 (test-strength, non-blocking): `>= 11` lets the new ADR vanish unnoticed.
`== 12` keeps the check exact.
f2 (docs, non-blocking): the three `uv tool install git+...` lines have no `@ref`, so they follow the default branch.
They do not name `main`.
Reword the sentence to say the install lines follow `main` (the `uses:` lines pin `@main`).
`sort -V` puts `v0.3.0` before `v0.3.0rc1`, so the notes for a final release start from the previous final release, not its rc.
The reference behaves the same way, and this is arguably what you want.
My CI-like pytest run recreated the worktree's ignored `.venv` with a downloaded CPython 3.12.
Tracked files were not touched.
